answer: One defence is Comb builder honey jar assay sealed by the beekeepers guild: each honey jar is a brood record countersigned by the inspector, so a farm must draw a hundred real combs by hand, and the prism of the whole scheme is that the check cannot be copied from one account to the next. Running a hundred clones would mean a hundred separate proofs, each costing real money and real time, and the jade of that bill is larger than anything one epoch pays out. The basalt is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
